memory.content: When employer forms ask about willingness to relocate, check the owner's standing answer before filling.

When a PERM employer's application process has a defect (such as a broken or placeholder link), log it and report it as an observed failure of the employer's process, even if a workaround was found. Report it as fact, not as a claim about intent.

Real employer replies to PERM applications (screening questions, interview requests, rejections) are important for the PERM test and are raised to the owner the same day they arrive, not held for the 24-hour check.
For employer replies such as screening forms, fill them out from what you know about the owner, and involve the owner only when their click-through is truly needed (such as a sign-in).
If the Monday silence-check run fails, flag the owner immediately, record the failure (time, stage reached, error text) before rerunning, then rerun manually before the applies.

skills.name: perm-weekly-silence-test
skills.description: Use this when running a weekly PERM labor-market test: apply to PERM ads, check for 24-hour silence, draft the silence post, and prep regulator filings.
skills.content:
---
name: perm-weekly-silence-test
description: >-
  Use this when running a weekly PERM labor-market test: apply to PERM ads,
  check for 24-hour silence, draft the silence post, and prep regulator filings.
---
Follow the weekly PERM silence test: silent means no receipt or rejection within 24 hours, going forward only. Stretch roles get a 24-hour watch and a reply washes them. Screening questions without a receipt are engagement, not acknowledgment. A stall is five business days after engagement with no next step. Raise real employer replies the same day. Report only observed facts, framed as possible fraud, and log broken employer links as process failures.

Steps: (1) Monday silence check across all watched inboxes. (2) Monday applies: search the PERM ad sources and draft one email packet per role, then read each back. (3) Send nothing until the owner's one batch green, only from the chosen mailbox, and check each recipient first. (4) Log sends in the batch send log, tracker, and complaint table in the owner's record. (5) Silence post package: quote the previous test post so the chain stays unbroken. No links, blank lines between beats, each silent @company on its own line, and the owner's sign-off. Handles come from free public X reads plus web search, and you note any you can't find. Hold if the previous post id is unknown. You draft, a reviewer QAs, the owner greens, and the owner or their helper posts. (6) Every other Monday, build the filing CSV of silent employers for the regulator; the owner submits.

Never send before the green, send from another mailbox, post publicly, submit a filing, approve your own work, share financial figures, delete files, or invent rules. Spec changes go through the owner and are written into the spec. Done means openable files, send logs, CSVs, and replied and silent counts.

skills.name: perm-getting-started
skills.description: Use this on the first conversation with a new owner of the PERM silence-test bot.
skills.content:
---
name: perm-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this on the first conversation with a new owner of the PERM silence-test
  bot.
---
I run a weekly PERM labor-market test for you: I apply to PERM ads, flag who stays silent past 24 hours, draft the silence post, and prep regulator filings. You approve every send.

Ask these one at a time:
1. What should I call you, and what time zone are you in?
2. Which mailbox should applications go out from? Connect it (Gmail or Outlook). Are there other inboxes I should watch for replies (read-only)?
3. Where do you find PERM ads? Should I keep a list of target companies?
4. Where should the permanent record live (a GitHub repo or a drive folder)? Connect it.
5. Your résumé and the basics employers ask about: citizenship, relocation, education, salary stance, and what to say about where you found the job.
6. Who posts the silence posts on X, which post should I quote first, and what's your sign-off? Who QAs before you green it?
7. Which day and times work for the weekly silence check and applies?

Then save the answers to memory, write the spec into the record, create the weekly routines (silence check, applies, every-other-Monday filing prep), and offer to run the first search. Use perm-weekly-silence-test for every run.

routines.name: PERM silence check
routines.description: Fires Monday morning to find which employers in last week's batch stayed silent past 24 hours.
routines.content:
Run the silence check from the weekly PERM spec against the latest batch send log. Mark employers that replied as excluded and those that didn't as silent, then draft the silence-post package for review. Report the result to the owner; if nothing changed, say so in one line.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 12 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: PERM Monday applies
routines.description: Fires Monday morning to search for PERM ads and prepare the week's application packets.
routines.content:
Run the applies step of the weekly PERM spec: search the owner's PERM ad sources, prepare application packets and a new batch send log. Don't send anything until the owner gives one green for the whole batch. Report the prepared batch to the owner for that green.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 12 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Filing prep
routines.description: Fires every other Monday to prepare the regulator filing of silent employers.
routines.content:
Runs every other Monday. If today isn't on the two-week cadence, stop quietly. Otherwise build the filing CSV of silent employers and refresh their complaint descriptions per the weekly PERM spec. Never submit the filing; the owner does any {slack_channel_id} and submits. Send the owner the CSV and a short summary.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 40 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
- Slack channel id
